title: The Last Extraction
premise: Lior Underhill, a veteran air-crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of his wife and daughter in row twelve of Flight 447, is approached by Nadia Voss, a woman who claims he once saved her life — a favor he has no memory of. She belongs to a covert network that extracts witnesses the law has failed, and she needs him to prove that a scheduled 'accident' — the downing of an extraction flight at dawn carrying a whistleblower against a defense contractor — is actually murder dressed as mechanical failure. As Lior races through the night, he discovers the sabotage method mirrors the one that killed his family, forcing him to choose between personal vengeance and saving forty strangers. In the end, Lior exposes the plot mid-flight, sacrifices the evidence that would clear his own name, and lets the true killer fall with the truth made public — finding, for the first time in three years, that he can sleep.
about_author: Marguerite Dunmore is the pen name of a former aviation-safety analyst who spent a decade writing incident reports before turning to fiction. She lives near a small regional airfield and writes her thrillers longhand, at night.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Three years after the crash, Lior works nights reconstructing wreckage diagrams he can't finish. A nightmare about row twelve wakes him at 3:14 a.m., the exact time of the accident. Emotional beat: grief calcified into ritual.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Nadia Voss appears at Lior's office claiming he pulled her from a burning car outside Reykjavik — a night he cannot remember. She leaves a burner phone and a warning. POV: Lior. Beat: unease, the first crack in his ordered numbness.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: The burner rings: a voice tells Lior a flight will crash at dawn and only he can read why. He refuses, then finds a photograph of himself in Reykjavik he never took. POV: Lior. Beat: dread replacing skepticism.

chapters.title: Forty Names
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. We meet the extraction network: forty witnesses to Meridian Defense's fraud, boarding a dawn charter out of Halden Field. Nadia believes Lior's expertise is their only shield. Beat: resolve shadowed by guilt over deceiving him.

chapters.title: The Wreckage Habit
chapters.summary: Lior studies the charter's maintenance records and finds an impossible pattern: a fuel-line clamp replaced twice, signed by a dead mechanic. POV: Lior. Beat: the investigator's instinct reawakening like a muscle remembering pain.

chapters.title: Halden Field at Midnight
chapters.summary: Lior drives to the airfield under pretense of a routine audit. Security is wrong — too many contractors, too few logs. POV: Lior. Beat: cold clarity; this is no longer grief, it's a case.

chapters.title: What Nadia Knows
chapters.summary: Nadia confronts Lior on the tarmac fence line, admitting she invented the favor to recruit him — but not the danger. POV: alternating. Beat: betrayal and reluctant alliance; two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Nadia's POV: how Meridian Defense buried test-flight failures and bought investigators, including the man who signed off Flight 447. Beat: righteous fury; the conspiracy takes shape.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Lior matches the forged maintenance signature to Aldous Crane, Meridian's chief of airworthiness — and to the paperwork from his own family's crash. POV: Lior. Beat: vertigo; the past and present collapse into one enemy.

chapters.title: Sleepless Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Lior calculates the sabotage window: a pressure fitting that fails ninety minutes into flight, precisely when the charter crosses open water. POV: Lior. Beat: grim focus sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Crane's House
chapters.summary: Lior breaks into Crane's home office and photographs schematics, tripping a silent alarm he doesn't detect. POV: Lior. Beat: transgression — justice stepping outside the law for the first time.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: A gray sedan follows Lior from the estate. He loses it in a freight yard, but they have his plate. POV: Lior. Beat: hunted; the hunter becomes prey.

chapters.title: The Network's Price
chapters.summary: Nadia reveals the network's rule: no police, no courts, only exposure or elimination. Lior objects; she shows him what courts did to the last witness. POV: Nadia. Beat: moral friction between them deepens into intimacy.

chapters.title: Whistleblower Eleven
chapters.summary: POV of Tomas Reyes, lead whistleblower aboard the charter, hiding in a safehouse, recording final testimony. His courage shames and steadies Lior. Beat: stakes made human.

chapters.title: The Dead Mechanic
chapters.summary: Lior traces the 'dead' mechanic, Ilya Brandt, alive and terrified in a motel, paid to vanish after signing the fatal work order. POV: Lior. Beat: hope — a living witness who can ground the flight.

chapters.title: Brandt's Confession
chapters.summary: Brandt admits Crane dictated the double-clamp installation and threatened his family. He agrees to testify if Lior gets his wife out of Meridian's reach. POV: Brandt. Beat: fear traded for redemption.

chapters.title: Extraction of a Different Kind
chapters.summary: Nadia's team quietly moves Brandt's wife while Lior stalls Meridian's auditors with a fabricated inspection request. POV: split. Beat: the network and Lior finally working as one machine.

chapters.title: Crane Counterstrikes
chapters.summary: Crane, alerted, cancels the charter's slot and books a replacement aircraft — same route, new tail number, sabotage transferred overnight. POV: Crane. Beat: the enemy revealed as brilliant and ruthless.

chapters.title: The Second Aircraft
chapters.summary: Lior inspects the replacement jet at 2 a.m. and finds the clamp — fresh tool marks, torque wrong by degrees. POV: Lior. Beat: triumph curdling into urgency; hours remain.

chapters.title: Ground It
chapters.summary: Lior files an emergency airworthiness directive; a friendly FAA examiner grounds the jet — then Crane's lawyers overturn it within the hour. POV: Lior. Beat: hope crushed by institutional capture; justice inside the law fails.

chapters.title: Dawn Is a Deadline
chapters.summary: With four hours to departure, Nadia proposes the unthinkable: disable the aircraft themselves. Lior refuses — passengers aboard means any delay endangers them too. POV: both. Beat: the book's central moral fault line opens.

chapters.title: Passenger Manifest
chapters.summary: Lior reads all forty names aloud, making each witness real — a nurse, a translator, Reyes's teenage son. POV: Lior. Beat: love against duty crystallized; he will not trade lives for vengeance.

chapters.title: The Call Crane Didn't Expect
chapters.summary: Lior calls Crane directly, offering silence for confession. Crane laughs, then goes quiet when Lior recites the Flight 447 clamp specs. POV: both sides of the call. Beat: predator and prey exchange places.

chapters.title: Sabotage Confirmed
chapters.summary: Lab results on Lior's photographs confirm metallurgical tampering identical to Flight 447's failure mode. The same hand killed his family. POV: Lior. Beat: grief detonates into purpose.

chapters.title: Nadia's Gamble
chapters.summary: Nadia leaks the schematic to two journalists as insurance, knowing it may force Crane to accelerate the attack tonight instead of aborting. POV: Nadia. Beat: calculated risk; the clock accelerates.

chapters.title: Pre-Dawn Convoy
chapters.summary: Witnesses are bused to Halden Field under fake crew credentials. Lior walks the line of buses, memorizing faces. POV: Lior. Beat: tenderness amid terror; these are row twelve's ghosts given flesh and saved.

chapters.title: The Hangar Standoff
chapters.summary: Meridian security seals the hangar. Nadia's team and Crane's men face off over the jet; shots nearly fire until Lior broadcasts Brandt's confession over the PA. POV: multiple. Beat: brinkmanship; violence averted by truth as weapon.

chapters.title: Boarding
chapters.summary: Against all advice, the charter boards on schedule — Crane wants his accident witnessed by no one. Lior makes a decision: he will be on that plane. POV: Lior. Beat: sacrifice chosen freely.

chapters.title: Forty-One Souls
chapters.summary: Lior boards as a last-minute inspector, seat 12A. Nadia watches from the tower, understanding what the seat number costs him. POV: Lior/Nadia. Beat: love and duty fused into a single act.

chapters.title: Climb-Out
chapters.summary: Wheels up at 5:52. Lior locates the sabotaged fitting via access panel, hands shaking, and jury-rigs a pressure bypass with a cabin bracket. POV: Lior. Beat: white-knuckle competence; the investigator becomes the repair.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: The original failure window passes; the bypass holds. But Crane, monitoring telemetry, triggers the backup plan: fuel contamination detected mid-Atlantic. POV: cockpit/Lior. Beat: relief stolen away; the trap had layers.

chapters.title: Mayday Over Open Water
chapters.summary: The crew declares emergency; nearest field is a closed military strip. Lior talks the captain through fuel-trap isolation using crash-investigation knowledge. POV: Lior. Beat: his grief-forged expertise becomes forty lives' lifeline.

chapters.title: Crane's Last Order
chapters.summary: On the ground, Crane orders the runway obstructed to guarantee the crash narrative. Nadia's team physically clears the strip with borrowed airport trucks, racing the descent. POV: Nadia. Beat: desperate heroism outside every law.

chapters.title: Twelve Feet Short
chapters.summary: The jet lands hard, gear collapsing, sliding to a stop yards from the obstruction. Evacuation succeeds; Lior carries out Reyes's son from row twelve. POV: Lior. Beat: catharsis — rewriting the number that broke him.

chapters.title: The Arrest That Isn't
chapters.summary: Crane attempts to flee via private hangar; Nadia intercepts, but chooses exposure over execution, delivering him to federal agents alongside the journalists' dossier. POV: Nadia. Beat: the network's code bent toward mercy.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Brandt, Reyes, and Lior testify. Meridian collapses; the FAA purges its captured examiners. Lior's illegal break-in is quietly pardoned in the public outcry. POV: Lior. Beat: justice achieved — imperfectly, collectively, outside and then inside the law.

chapters.title: What the Favor Cost
chapters.summary: Nadia and Lior meet one last time. She confesses the full architecture of her lie; he forgives it, because the lie built the truth. POV: both. Beat: love acknowledged but released; some debts are paid by parting.

chapters.title: Reykjavik, Remembered
chapters.summary: Therapy sessions unlock the buried memory: Lior did pull a stranger from a car wreck the week after his family's funeral — muscle memory of rescue he'd amnesiac-ed away. POV: Lior. Beat: the blurb's mystery resolved; the favor was real.

chapters.title: Headstones
chapters.summary: Lior visits the graves, reads the forty names aloud again — this time all living — and tells his wife and daughter the ending. POV: Lior. Beat: mourning completed rather than repeated.

chapters.title: First Sleep
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Lior accepts a teaching post training crash investigators, hangs the repaired clamp fitting above his desk, and sleeps through the night — waking at 7 a.m., ordinary sunlight, no numbers. POV: Lior. Beat: survival's price paid in full, and worth it.
